items.title: Jerome Richardson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 9, 1996
items.q: And so I heard, much later, that Herbie Mann was supposed to have done the first flute solo, or Frank Wess. So I don't know.

ctx.x: That’s quite a marketing philosophy. Well you recorded one of the first flute solos, didn’t you? With Lionel Hampton?

I think so. There is controversy about that one. This was back in 1949. Quincy Jones wrote a piece called “Kingfish.” And that was an odd one too in that we were rehearsing that and there was only I think about eight or ten pieces playing that particular piece. And my wife called, we were in I think Kansas City or somewhere, and my wife called from Berkeley. And I told Bobby Plater I said, “Bobby, play my part.” And I was playing alto in the band at that time. And so I talked to my wife and I came back and I…
Because the things always weren’t released as soon as —

items.title: Frank Wess interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 29, 1995
items.q: Jerome Richardson was playing... whenever we ran into each other we used to play duets together

ctx.x: What was the audience response like? Did they like it?

Oh, yeah, yeah. Well I mean it was different, you know, ‘cause wasn’t nobody really doing that. Sam Most was playing, and Jerome Richardson was playing, but you know, nobody had really heard that really. Sam Most had done some things with, I forget who it was, one of the bands. It might have been Don Redman, I don’t know. Because we used to, whenever they would come to watch, and whenever we ran into each other we used to play duets together, you know, and things. But there really wasn’t too much of it around,…
We’ve been interested in seeing if we can give some of our students an idea of what it must have been like to live on the road, and you did a couple of different periods of it.
